question:
A pipe can fill a water tank in 36 minutes, and another can fill it in 48 minutes, but a third pipe can empty it in 18 minutes.

The first two pipes are kept open for 16 minutes at the beginning, and then the third pipe is also opened. How long does it take to empty the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let total capacity of the tank be LCM(36, 48, 18) = 144 units.

Efficiency: A = +4 units/min, B = +3 units/min, C = −8 units/min.

Water filled by A and B in 16 minutes = 16 × (4 + 3) = 112 units.

Net efficiency when A, B and C are open = 4 + 3 − 8 = −1 unit/min.

Time required to empty the filled 112 units = 112 ÷ 1 = 112 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 112 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by pipe A to fill the tank = 36 minutes

Time taken by pipe B to fill the tank = 48 minutes

Time taken by pipe C to empty the tank = 18 minutes

Pipes A and B are kept open for 16 minutes initially.

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Total Work is taken as the LCM of time taken by individual pipes.

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Minutes**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 36
 144
 +4
 
 

 B
 48
 +3
 
 

 C
 18
 −8
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity of the tank = LCM of 36, 48 and 18 = 144 units

⇒ Volume filled by pipes A and B in 1 minute = 4 + 3 = 7 units

⇒ Volume filled by pipes A and B in 16 minutes = 7 × 16 = 112 units

⇒ After 16 minutes, pipe C is also opened.

⇒ Net efficiency of all three pipes A, B, and C = 4 + 3 − 8 = −1 unit/minute

⇒ A negative efficiency indicates that the tank will be emptied at a rate of 1 unit per minute.

⇒ Time taken to empty the 112 units already filled = 112 ÷ 1 = 112 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 112 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Principle

It operates on the exact same logic as Time & Work. The entire tank capacity acts as the Total Work.

Negative Efficiency (Leak or Outlet Pipe)

Inlet pipes add to the volume (+ efficiency), while outlet pipes or leaks remove volume (− efficiency). Net flow is the algebraic sum of all active pipes.

Filling vs. Emptying Conclusion

If the net efficiency is positive, the tank gets filled. If negative, whatever volume is currently present will get emptied over time.

question: Ajit and Bimal can do a piece of work in 5, and 8 days, respectively, while Chandan can destroy the same work in 12 days. Ajit works on the 1st day, Bimal works on the 2nd day, Chandan works on the 3rd day and so on. They follow the same pattern until the work gets completed. How many days will it take for the work to be completed the first time?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Total Work = LCM(5, 8, 12) = 120 units.

1 cycle (3 days) work = Ajit + Bimal + Chandan = 24 + 15 − 10 = 29 units.

Work completed in 3 full cycles (9 days) = 3 × 29 = 87 units.

On 10th day, Ajit adds 24 units ⇒ Total work = 87 + 24 = 111 units.

Remaining 9 units are done by Bimal on 11th day in 9 ÷ 15 = 3/5 day.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 ³/₅ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Ajit = 5 days

Time taken by Bimal = 8 days

Time taken by Chandan (destroying work) = 12 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of time taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Ajit
 5
 120
 24
 
 

 Bimal
 8
 15
 
 

 Chandan
 12
 −10
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done in a 3-day cycle = 24 + 15 − 10 = 29 units.

⇒ In alternating positive-negative work, reserve the peak positive capacity to avoid over-calculating.

⇒ Peak positive continuous work in a cycle = 24 (Ajit) + 15 (Bimal) = 39 units.

⇒ Work to complete safely using full cycles = 120 − 39 = 81 units.

⇒ Number of full 3-day cycles needed = 81 ÷ 29 ≈ 2.79 ⇒ safely take 3 full cycles.

⇒ Work done in 3 cycles (9 days) = 3 × 29 = 87 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 120 − 87 = 33 units.

⇒ On the 10th day, Ajit works and completes 24 units.

⇒ Work left after 10 days = 33 − 24 = 9 units.

⇒ On the 11th day, Bimal works. Time taken by Bimal = 9 ÷ 15 = 3/5 day.

⇒ Total time taken = 10 + 3/5 = 10 ³/₅ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 ³/₅ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternating Work with Negative Efficiency

When positive and negative work alternate, always subtract the maximum positive continuous work from the total work. Use the remaining work to find the number of full cycles needed to safely approach completion without exceeding the total work.

Total Work using LCM

For multiple individuals working at different rates, Total Work is assumed to be the LCM of their individual time to ensure calculations remain in whole numbers, and Efficiency is calculated as Total Work ÷ Time.

question: A train can travel 50% faster than a car. Both start from point A at the same time and reach point B, 60 km away from point A, at the same time. On the way, however, the train lost about 12.5 min while stopping at the stations. The speed of the car is:
solution:
**Given :**

Speed of train is 50% faster than car 

Distance between point A and B = 60 km

Time taken by train is to cover 60 km = (t - 12.5) minutes or (t - 12.5)/60 hours

Time taken by car to cover 60 km = t minutes or t/60 hours 

**Formula Used :**

Speed = Distance/time 

**Calculations :**

Let the speed of car be S

Speed of train is 50% more than car = S + 50% of S = (3/2)S

Now for train 

⇒ 60 = (3/2)S × (t - 12.5)/60 ...(1)

Now for car 

⇒ 60 = S × (t/60) ...(2)

Solving both equations

value of t = (75/2) minutes or (5/8) hours 

Speed of car = distance/Speed 

⇒ 60/(5/8)

⇒ 96 km/hours 

∴ **The speed of the car is 96 km/hour** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** Here, 50% = 1/2. So, Ratio of speed of train to car = 3 : 2 ⇒ 3x and 2x respectively

Now, Let the time taken by car = t hours,

Then the time taken by train = t -12.5min = t - 12.5/60 h

⇒ (t -5/24)h

Since distances are equal 

⇒ 3x × ( t - 5/24) = 2x × t

⇒ 3t - 5/8 = 2t

⇒ t = 5/8 h

Now, speed of car = Distance/Time = 60 ÷ 5/8

⇒ 60 × 8/5 = 96km/h

question: The distance between a man and a 230m long train is 115 m. How much time (in seconds) will the train, which is running at a speed of 60 km/h, take to pass the man who is running at a speed of 9 km/h towards the train?

question: Two trains starting at the same time from two stations 300 km apart and going in opposite directions cross each other at a distance of 180 km from one of the stations. What is the ratio of speeds of faster train to slower train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When travel time is constant, Speed is directly proportional to Distance.

Distance covered by the faster train = 180 km

Distance covered by the slower train = 300 − 180 = 120 km

Ratio of speeds = Ratio of distances = 180 : 120

Speed Ratio = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance between the two stations = 300 km

Distance covered by the faster train before crossing = 180 km

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bab2e62bc296011a93d54715b26f8bdf935eabac2f62a02ba88e5fae74c5ce54.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by the slower train = 300 − 180 = 120 km

⇒ Since both trains start at the same time and cross each other, the time traveled by both is perfectly equal.

⇒ Let the time taken be t hours.

⇒ Speed of faster train = 180 ÷ t

⇒ Speed of slower train = 120 ÷ t

⇒ Ratio of speeds = (180 ÷ t) : (120 ÷ t)

⇒ Ratio of speeds = 180 : 120

⇒ Speed ratio = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions)

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). The time taken for them to meet is Total Distance ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Constant Time Principle

When the travel time is constant for two moving bodies, the ratio of their speeds is directly proportional to the ratio of the distances they cover: S₁ ÷ S₂ = D₁ ÷ D₂.

Constant Distance Principle

When the distance covered is constant for two moving bodies, their speeds are inversely proportional to the time taken: S₁ ÷ S₂ = T₂ ÷ T₁.
</p

question: Train A passes an electric pole in 15 seconds, moving at 60 kmh. It crosses train B moving in the opposite direction at 48 km/h, in 19 seconds. What is the length (in m) of train B?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Length of Train A = Speed × Time = (60 × 5/18) × 15 = 250 m

Relative speed (opposite direction) = (60 + 48) × 5/18 = 108 × 5/18 = 30 m/s

Total distance (Length of Train A + Length of Train B) = Relative speed × Time = 30 × 19 = 570 m

Length of Train B = 570 − 250 = 320 m

**∴ The correct answer is 320 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Speed of Train A (SA) = 60 km/h

Time taken by Train A to cross an electric pole = 15 s

Speed of Train B (SB) = 48 km/h

Time taken by both trains to cross each other = 19 s

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

Relative Speed (opposite directions) = SA + SB

**Calculations:**

 60 km/h →
 Length = 250 m

 ← 48 km/h
 Length = ?

⇒ Speed of Train A in m/s = 60 × 5/18 = 50/3 m/s

⇒ Length of Train A (LA) = Speed × Time = (50/3) × 15 = 250 m

⇒ Relative speed of Train A and Train B = 60 + 48 = 108 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 108 × 5/18 = 30 m/s

⇒ Total distance covered during crossing = LA + LB

⇒ Total Distance = Relative speed × Time

⇒ 250 + LB = 30 × 19

⇒ 250 + LB = 570

⇒ LB = 570 − 250 = 320 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions)

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Concepts

When a train crosses a stationary object of negligible length (like an electric pole or a standing man), the distance traveled is equal to the length of the train itself. When crossing another train or a platform, the distance traveled is the sum of their lengths: L₁ + L₂.

question: Two trains A and B are running in the same direction at the uniform speeds of 80 km/h and 100 km/h, respectively. Train A leaves the station 30 min earlier than the train B from the same station. The time taken by train B to cross train A will be:
solution:
**Given:-**

Speed of train A = 80 km/h

Speed of train B = 100km/h

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:-**

Let, the time taken to cross-train A is T hr.

According to the question, A leaves the station 30 min earlier 

Distance traveled by A in 30 min (i.e. (1)/(2) hr) = 80 × (1)/(2) = 40 km.

Distance traveled by A in T hr = 80T

Distance traveled by B in T hr = 100T 

Train B will cross train A if 

100 T = 80 T + 40

⇒ 20T = 40

⇒ T = 2 hours

So, **Train B will take 2 hours to pass train A.**

Distance travel in first 1 hour = 40 + 80 = 120 km

Distance travel in next 1 hour = 200 + 80 = 280 km

For train B -

Distance travel in first 1 hour = 100km

Distance travel in next 1 hour = 100 + 100 = 200 km

So, **Train B passes the train A in 2 hours.**

question: The speed of a train was increasing by 3 km/h after every one hour for up to 10 hours and then, it was increasing by 5 km/h. If the distance traveled in the first one hour was 40 km. what was the total distance covered by the train in 20 hours?
solution:
**Given:**

The speed of a train was increasing by 3 km/h after every one hour for up to 10 hours.

After 10 hrs it was increasing by 5 km/h.

The distance traveled in the first one hour was 40 km.

**Concept used:**

Distance = speed × time

**Calculation:**

For first 1 hour speed is 40 km/h.

The speed of a train was increasing by 3 km/h after every one hour .

So for the next nine hours speed will be 43,46,49,52,55,58,61,64,and 67

Total distance covered in 1st 10 hours = 43 + 46 + 49 + 52 + 55 + 58 + 61 + 64 + 67 = 535 km

So for the next 10 hours speed will be 72 ,77,82,87, 92,97,102,107,112,117

The total distance covered in next 10 hrs will be 72 + 77 + 82 + 87 + 92 + 97 + 102 + 107 + 112 + 117 = 945 km

So total distance covered in 20 hrs will be 945 + 535 = 1480 km

**The total distance covered by the train in 20 hours is 1480 km**

question: A train starts from station P, runs through stations Q, R, S, T and reaches station U. It stops at stations Q, R, S and T for 2 minutes, 4 minutes, 6 minutes, and 8 minutes, respectively. The distance between P and U is 50 km. What is the average speed of the train between stations P and U (in km/h), if it runs for 70 minutes between the stations, with uniform speed?
solution:
**Given:**

Distance = 50 km,

Total run time = 70 minutes,

Stoppage time at stations = 2 + 4 + 6 + 8 = 20 minutes

**Concept:**

Average speed = Total distance/Total time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total time including stoppages = 70 + 20 = 90 minutes = 90/60 = 1.5 hours

⇒ Average speed = 50 km/1.5 hours = 100/3 km/h

**Hence, the average speed of the train between stations P and U is 100/3 km/h.**
